headline: Legal Affairs Dept Holds E-Waste Awareness Workshop under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Law and Justice

Legal Affairs Dept Holds E-Waste Awareness Workshop under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

29 SEP 2026 10:08PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 29 September 2026: As part of Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the Department of Legal Aﬀairs organized an awareness workshop on ‘E-waste Management’ at Kartavya Bhavan-2, New Delhi, on 28 September 2026.

The workshop was attended by Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Department of Legal Aﬀairs, along with officers and officials of the Department. The workshop aimed to sensitise participants about the growing importance of responsible management of electronic waste and encourage environmentally sustainable practices in day-to-day life and workplace.

Addressing the participants, Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Department of Legal Aﬀairs, highlighted the importance of responsible e-waste management and emphasised the need for greater awareness regarding the proper handling and disposal of electronic waste. He stressed the significance of adopting sustainable practices and collective responsibility to minimise the adverse impact of e-waste on the environment.

The workshop provided participants with useful information on various aspects of e-waste management, including proper segregation, safe collection, responsible disposal and recycling of electronic items. The participants were also sensitised to the 3R approach — Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, which encourages reducing the generation of e-waste, reusing electronic products wherever feasible and ensuring their recycling through appropriate channels.

The session also highlighted the importance of responsible disposal of discarded electronic devices and components, while creating awareness about the environmental benefits of adopting sustainable consumption and waste-management practices.

The awareness initiative forms part of the Department’s eﬀorts under Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 to promote cleanliness, sustainability and responsible waste management. It also reinforced the message that eﬀective e-waste management requires active participation and awareness at both the individual and institutional levels.

The Department of Legal Aﬀairs remains committed to promoting a cleaner, greener and more sustainable workplace through awareness, responsible practices and active participation of its officers and officials.

headline: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Felicitates 20 Award-Winning Artists at National Exhibition of Arts
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Felicitates 20 Award-Winning Artists at National Exhibition of Arts

65th National Art Exhibition Receives Over 6,000 Entries; 270 Artists Selected Through Two-Tier Jury Process

29 SEP 2026 9:42PM by PIB Delhi

The 65th National Exhibition of Art, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi, was held on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Government of India, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India; Shri K.K. Mishra, Joint Secretary (Akademies), Ministry of Culture; and Shri Rajeev Kumar, Secretary, Lalit Kala Akademi, along with Padma Shri awardees Shri Sudhakar Olwe, Shri Sudarshan Patnaik, and Shri Ashok Kumar Vishwas were present on the occasion.

On the occasion, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and other dignitaries viewed artworks created from waste materials during the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ workshops organised at various centres of the Lalit Kala Akademi.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat highlighted the significance of bringing together creativity and sustainability. He said that the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ initiative, organised on the occasion of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday, demonstrates how creativity and the spirit of service can come together meaningfully. He appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi’s efforts across its various verticals, including the ‘Waste to Wonder’ initiative, which gives discarded materials a new artistic expression and highlights the role of art in promoting sustainability.

Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, highlighted the importance of providing wider opportunities and greater visibility to artists and contemporary Indian art. He invited members of the public, art enthusiasts and visitors to view the 65th National Exhibition of Art at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, which has been extended until October 31, 2026. He encouraged people to visit the exhibition and experience the diverse artistic expressions and contemporary trends represented by artists from across the country.

Shri Rajeev Kumar, Secretary, Lalit Kala Akademi, highlighted the national reach and evolution of the National Exhibition of Art. He said that the 65th edition received more than 6,000 entries, out of which 270 artists were selected through a two-tier jury process. He also highlighted the awards presented as part of the exhibition and the Akademi’s continued efforts to recognise and promote artistic talent from across the country.

A monograph on Abdul Aziz Raiba, edited by Shri Ram Gopal Khadilkar, was also released on the occasion. An eminent modern Indian painter, Raiba was known for his bold lines, vibrant colours and distinctive fusion of Indian traditional and modern art.

During the programme, the Union Minister felicitated 20 award-winning artists. The awards recognise their creative contributions to the field of Indian visual arts.

Following the programme, the Chief Guest and other dignitaries visited the National Exhibition of Art at the Lalit Kala Gallery. The exhibition reflects the Lalit Kala Akademi’s continued endeavour to recognise, promote and provide wider visibility to artistic talent from different parts of the country.

headline: India and Republic of Korea Hold 10th Joint Committee Meeting on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation

Ministry of Defence

India and Republic of Korea Hold 10th Joint Committee Meeting on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation

29 SEP 2026 9:31PM by PIB Delhi

The 10th India-Republic of Korea Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation was held in New Delhi on September 29, 2026. Both countries reviewed the ongoing bilateral cooperation in defence industries and logistics and discussed avenues to further strengthen and expand defence ties.

The discussions provided an opportunity to exchange views on enhancing cooperation between the defence industries of the two countries and promoting greater engagement in defence production and logistics.

The meeting was co-chaired by Shri Dinesh Mahur, Additional Secretary (Defence Production), Ministry of Defence, and Mr. Kim Il Dong, Vice Minister, Defence Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea.

Mr. Seong Ho Lee, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, and Dr. Vijay Namdeorao Zade, Joint Secretary (Naval Systems), Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, also attended the meeting along with senior officials from both countries.

Representatives of leading defence companies from both countries also participated. M/s Larsen & Toubro (L&T) and M/s Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) participated in the discussions. Republic of Korea was represented by Hanwha Aerospace, Korean Air, Hanwha Systems, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) and DS Navcours.

On the sidelines of the JCM, Vice Minister, Defence Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea, Mr. Kim Il Dong, called on Hon’ble Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth. During the interaction, both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral defence cooperation and deepening collaboration in defence industries and logistics.

The 10th JCM reaffirmed the close and growing defence ties between India and the Republic of Korea and provided an important platform for advancing bilateral cooperation in defence production and logistics.

headline: NRIDA and IIM Kolkata Sign MoU for Four-Year Impact Assessment Study of PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

NRIDA and IIM Kolkata Sign MoU for Four-Year Impact Assessment Study of PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN

Four-Year Study to Assess Long-Term Socio-Economic Impact of Rural Roads under PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN

29 SEP 2026 9:14PM by PIB Delhi

The National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA), Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, and the Indian Institute of Management Kolkata (IIM Kolkata) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for undertaking a comprehensive four-year longitudinal Impact Assessment Study of roads constructed under PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN.

The MoU was signed by Ms Aditi Singh (IAS) Director General, NRIDA, on behalf of NRIDA, Ministry of Rural Development Government of India and Prof. Alok Kumar Rai Director, (IIM Kolkata), in the presence of Secretary, Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal and other officials of Ministry and IIM Kolkata marking an important step towards strengthening evidence-based impact assessment of rural connectivity interventions.

Key Highlights of the Study

Four-year longitudinal impact assessment to assess the long-term outcomes of rural road connectivity.

Coverage of 10 States/UTs, 50 districts, 150 blocks and 250 roads. States/UT’s to be covered are Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Jammu & Kashmir, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Uttarakhand.

Survey of approximately 5,000 households to assess changes in mobility, accessibility and socio-economic conditions.

The study will follow a longitudinal approach involving Baseline Survey (Pre-Construction Survey) and Endline Survey (Post Construction Survey) data collection to assess changes over time.

Assessment of the impact of rural roads on mobility, accessibility, socio-economic conditions and access to essential services.

Baseline Survey (Pre Construction Survey): 14 months

Transition Period: Approximately 12 months

Endline Survey (Post Construction Survey): 22 months

Expected Outcomes

The long-term study is expected to generate robust evidence on the sustained socio-economic and developmental impacts of rural road connectivity under PMGSY-IV and PM-JANMAN. It will assess how improved connectivity influences accessibility and mobility, livelihoods, employment, income diversification, agriculture, non-farm activities and access to markets as well as household welfare and rural deprivation.

The study will also assess the long-term impact of improved rural road connectivity on education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, safety, and access to essential public and financial services. Particular emphasis will be given to changes observed in travel time and transportation costs, mobility, access to employment and livelihood opportunities and migration patterns. It will further examine changes in these outcomes over time and assess variations across different regions and vulnerable groups, thereby, providing a comprehensive understanding of the long-term impact of rural road connectivity.

An important outcome will be the assessment of the sustainability of these benefits in ensuring continued socio-economic gains. The proposed study may help in identifying implementation gaps, emerging challenges and areas requiring policy intervention.

Overall, the collaboration between NRIDA, MoRD and IIM Kolkata will provide valuable inputs for programme review, outcome monitoring, evidence-based policy formulation and future planning in rural infrastructure development.

headline: UIDAI unveils five new initiatives at Aadhaar Samvaad Kolkata to further advance trusted digital identity and good governance
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

UIDAI unveils five new initiatives at Aadhaar Samvaad Kolkata to further advance trusted digital identity and good governance

Hon’ble MoS Sh Jitin Prasada said Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story and emphasized the role of Aadhaar in improving ease of living

Over 600 senior policy makers, industry players and innovators came together to deliberate the way forward

29 SEP 2026 8:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) today conducted a day long stakeholders conference with ecosystem partners to deliberate and share ideas to further enhance service delivery, improve convenience by using Aadhaar and contribute to the larger good of people.

Over 600 stakeholders including senior policy makers, industry leaders, technocrats, and professionals came together for the ‘Aadhaar Samvaad’ in Kolkata, which coincided with the 17th Aadhaar Day.

The event was graced by Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State, Ministry of Commerce and Industry and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology as the chief guest and marked an important milestone in Aadhaar's continuing evolution as a trusted digital identity infrastructure for India.

“Aadhaar is a great success story. Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story,” Prasada said.

“Aadhaar has been instrumental in enhancing service delivery, promoting mass scale financial inclusion, and ensuring that government benefits, reach the right people. As a cornerstone of our digital governance, Aadhaar has revolutionized the way we access government services, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and inclusivity,” Prasada added, and underlined the importance of staying in sync with the emerging technologies.

He also underlined how Aadhaar is going to be beneficial for the people of West Bengal and benefits will reach the right beneficiaries of government initiatives.

CEO UIDAI Sh Saurabh Vijay said resident continues to remain at the centre of every action of UIDAI and Aadhaar ecosystem. He underlined that the product launches on the 17th Aadhaar Day is in sync with this resident centricity philosophy.

“Throughout the day, we discussed with our stakeholders on issues like expanding usage of Aadhaar, further strengthening authentication ecosystem for good governance, the enrolment and update ecosystem, and challenges and opportunities of emerging technologies,” Vijay said.

“Today is also an occasion to recognise that Aadhaar continues to evolve with the changing needs of a rapidly transforming digital India. New technologies, new forms of service delivery and stronger emphasis on privacy, security and resident convenience are shaping its next chapter,” said Vivek C Verma, Deputy Director General, UIDAI in his welcome address.

The occasion witnessed the launch of five new initiatives aimed at enhancing resident convenience, strengthening security, enabling good governance and preparing the Aadhaar ecosystem for the next phase of digital transformation.

A key launch was Face Authentication for the Electronic Public Distribution System (ePDS), jointly undertaken by UIDAI, the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC). The consent-based, contactless authentication option provides beneficiaries with an additional mode of authentication, particularly in situations where fingerprint authentication may be difficult, and enables States and Union Territories to integrate Face Authentication into their ePDS ecosystems.

UIDAI also launched SWIK Portal 2.0, which streamlines the process for seeking approval for Aadhaar authentication under the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance framework. Eligible non-Government entities can now submit proposals for permissible use cases directly through the portal to the concerned Ministry/Department, enabling a structured and coordinated approval process. https://swik.meity.gov.in/

The Sub-AUA/Sub-KUA (LITE) Framework launched today will facilitate wider adoption of Aadhaar authentication by Government and eligible other than Government entities with low-volume requirements. Eligible entities can leverage the authentication infrastructure of an existing AUA/KUA, enabling simpler and faster onboarding in real time without establishing any authentication infrastructure, while adhering to UIDAI’s security, privacy and regulatory requirements.

UIDAI also unveiled a new Token Management System, which will make it easier for people to go to state and regional offices of UIDAI for services wherever applicable.

Revamped UIDAI website:

Prasad unveiled a revamped UIDAI website, which will make information flow real time on its website. Residents come to UIDAI for four fundamental reasons: understand Aadhaar, access a service, find a document, or seek assistance. The redesigned website brings these journeys into a clearer structure.

The website has been designed in alignment with the Aadhaar brand guidelines, establishing a consistent visual identity across the UIDAI website, the myAadhaar portal and the Aadhaar App.

Accessibility has been a key consideration in the design of the revamped website. It incorporates features such as screen-reader compatibility, adjustable font sizes, improved colour contrast, keyboard navigation, and other accessibility enhancements to make Aadhaar-related information and services more accessible and inclusive for all residents, including persons with disabilities.

With BHASHINI integration, the website supports 13 languages, including English and Hindi. We are planning to make the website available in 23 languages in near future – up from 13 today.

The revamped website also introduces the UIDAI Career Portal, enabling online applications for deputation opportunities and providing a more streamlined and transparent process for prospective applicants.

headline: “By treating the landscape, twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation can be achieved”- Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

“By treating the landscape, twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation can be achieved”- Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan

29 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

Department of Land Resources organised a National Workshop on proposed Pilot projects on River Rejuvenation through the watershed approach, at New Delhi on 29 September 2026.

Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, emphasised that river rejuvenation requires treating the landscapes that feed rivers, with interventions tailored to the specific hydrological conditions of each catchment.

The Workshop brought together hydrologists, groundwater experts, geospatial scientists from IITs, experts from ICAR Institutes, National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Central Ground Water Board, NMCG, National River Conservation Directorate (NRCD), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, National Institute of Hydrology (NIH), National Geophysical Research Institute, Watershed practitioners, State Government representatives, research institutions, NGOs and International Organisations to deliberate on a scientific framework for river rejuvenation through watershed development.

Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, stated that the proposed pilots will focus on restoring river hydrology through catchment treatment, groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation, and improvement of base and lean-season flows.

He emphasised that “River/Streams Rejuvenation through Watershed Development Approach” can achieve twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation. We need to scientifically understand the hydrology of each catchment and establish whether targeted interventions can restore the lost hydrological function of a river or stream.”

He emphasised that planning should be based on a hydrological baseline, including rainfall, groundwater, catchment condition and water balance.

CEO, National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), Dr. Chandra Shekhar Kumar, as Chief Guest of the programme, said, “For small rivers, where long-term flow data is often limited, we need a systematic data-based framework that brings together legacy data, scientific analysis, high-resolution mapping and Decision Support Systems to guide river selection and treatment planning.”

Joint Secretary, Watershed Management, DoLR, Shri Nitin Khade, said, “The objective of these pilots is to increase river flows through groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation and intensive watershed treatment, while simultaneously improving agricultural productivity and income of farmers residing in the catchment areas. The challenge is to achieve both objectives in a balanced manner.”

Shri Khade said that the proposed pilots will focus on first-, second-, and third-order streams, with selection based on parameters including historical decline in flow, catchment condition, rainfall, groundwater depletion, intervention potential and data availability.

The workshop also highlighted the importance of convergence with government programmes and schemes, including VB-G RAM G, CAMPA, Ministry of Jal Shakti and State schemes and programmes, CSR, NGOs, along with support from research institutions and international organisations. The workshop emphasized on giving effect to Whole of Government and Whole of Society Approach.

The workshop deliberated on river selection, hydrological baselines, catchment treatment, GIS and remote sensing, intervention design, institutional frameworks, multidisciplinary teams, monitoring and evaluation, convergence, community participation and long-term maintenance.

The proposed monitoring framework will assess outcomes across four dimensions: Hydrological, Environmental, Agricultural and Socio-economic, with the objective of generating evidence that can guide the potential scaling up of watershed development approach based river rejuvenation across the country.

headline: Dr. L. Murugan Highlights Role of Creator Economy and AI in Building Viksit Bharat at YouTube Impact Summit 2026
fullText:

Dr. L. Murugan Highlights Role of Creator Economy and AI in Building Viksit Bharat at YouTube Impact Summit 2026

Technology May Change Rapidly, But Constitutional Values Must Endure: Dr. L. Murugan’s Message to Young Creators at YouTube Impact Summit 2026

Over 18,000 Indian YouTube Channels Have Crossed One Million Subscribers, Reflecting Growing Creator Economy

29 SEP 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi

Urging young creators to harness artificial intelligence as a tool for innovation and empowerment, Dr. L. Murugan, Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, said, “The future should not be: AI versus creators. It should be: AI empowering creators.” Calling upon young creators to “Create with courage. Create with responsibility. Create with purpose,” he emphasised that while “Technology changes rapidly. Constitutional values endure.”

India is not merely a nation of more than a billion people; we are a nation of more than a billion stories, ideas and aspirations.

Delighted to deliver the keynote address at the #YouTubeImpactSummit 2026.

YouTube’s contribution of over ₹18,000 crore to India’s GDP and support… pic.twitter.com/1Ov7DH5uhw

— Dr.L.Murugan (@DrLMurugan) September 29, 2026

Addressing the YouTube Impact Summit 2026, themed “Co-Creating Impact: India’s Digital Leadership and the Orange Economy”, in New Delhi today, the Minister highlighted the growing role of India’s digital and creative economy in driving economic growth, employment and global cultural outreach. The Summit brought together policymakers, technology leaders, creators, entrepreneurs and innovators, with Dr. L. Murugan delivering the keynote address.

Creator Economy Driving Growth and Employment

According to the YouTube Impact Report unveiled at the Summit, YouTube’s creative ecosystem contributed more than ₹18,000 crore to India’s GDP in 2025 and supported over 9.6 lakh full-time-equivalent jobs across the country.

The Minister noted that content produced in India receives over 15 per cent of its watch time from audiences outside India, while more than 18,000 Indian YouTube channels have crossed one million subscribers.

From Digital India to Creative India

Dr. Murugan highlighted India’s digital transformation through digital payments, digital public infrastructure, startups, artificial intelligence, affordable connectivity and digital education. He emphasised the need to move from consumers to creators, users to innovators and content consumption to intellectual-property creation.

He said digital technology has changed the geography of opportunity, enabling talent from every district, language and community to reach global audiences.

Strengthening the Orange Economy

Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Create in India, Create for the World,” the Minister highlighted the Orange Economy’s three pillars content, creativity and culture.

He said creativity extends beyond entertainment and can generate jobs, businesses, intellectual property, exports and cultural influence.

AI to Empower, Not Replace, Creators

Dr. Murugan said AI can assist creators in writing, translation, editing, animation, composition, design and distribution, while human imagination remains central to creativity.

He reiterated that AI should empower creators rather than replace them, while stressing the need for accessible, responsible and ethical use of emerging technologies.

The Summit also featured the unveiling of “Create with AI” films, developed in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT).

Government Initiatives for Creative Talent

The Minister highlighted initiatives including WAVES, IICT, Create in India Challenges, Gems of India, WAVES Bazaar, MyWAVES and Creator’s Corner to strengthen pathways for identifying, developing and connecting creative talent with markets.

He also highlighted the Union Budget 2026–27 provision for AVGC content-creator laboratories in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges. He noted that the industry is projected to require nearly 2 million professionals by 2030.

Constitutional Values in the Digital Age

Emphasising that “Technology changes rapidly. Constitutional values endure,” Dr. Murugan highlighted the relevance of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity in India’s digital transformation.

Referring to Article 19 and the freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable constitutional restrictions, he stressed that the freedom to create must be accompanied by responsibility.

He also highlighted Fundamental Duties under Article 51A, calling for responsible creation, sharing, verification and innovation in the digital age.

Taking India’s Stories to the World

Dr. Murugan emphasised that India’s cultural heritage can reach new audiences through cinema, music, gaming, animation, digital storytelling, design, crafts and literature.

Addressing young creators, he said their language, culture and stories can be global and urged them to create with confidence in India’s diversity.

The Minister said that the future of India’s digital economy will depend on what the country creates with technology, stressing the importance of employment, intellectual property, global opportunities and inclusive growth towards Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Summit highlighted the growing role of India’s digital and creative industries in advancing Viksit Bharat 2047, with the Minister calling for collective efforts to build an inclusive and globally competitive creative ecosystem. Ms. Gunjan Soni, Country Managing Director, YouTube India; Ms. Leslie Miller, Vice President, Global Government Affairs and Public Policy, YouTube; and Shri Senthil Rajan, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, were also present.

headline: Union Environment Minister honours India’s Environmental Champions at 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026, calls Conservation a National Responsibility
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Union Environment Minister honours India’s Environmental Champions at 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026, calls Conservation a National Responsibility

Senior IFS Officer Shri B. K. Singh receives Lifetime Achievement Award; 15 Forest Officers honoured for exemplary contribution to Environmental Conservation

29 SEP 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today presided over the 4th Eco Warrior Awards and Eco Warrior Conclave, organised by the Indian Forest Service Association (IFSA) and Indian Masterminds, in New Delhi. The event brought together senior forest officers, conservationists, policymakers, scientists, civil society representatives and industry representatives to recognise outstanding contributions to forest, wildlife and environmental conservation.

Honoured India’s environmental champions at the 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026 in New Delhi today.

From beat guards and rangers to frontline forest personnel, they protect our forests, respond to fires and safeguard wildlife habitats—turning conservation policy into action on the… pic.twitter.com/3V1WLhItIg

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) September 29, 2026

Addressing the event, Shri Yadav said India’s forests are vital ecological infrastructure supporting water, climate, soil, biodiversity and livelihoods. He also recognised frontline forest personnel and stressed the role of tribal and forest-dependent communities as conservation partners. The Minister said conservation has become more complex, with forest officers required to manage entire ecological landscapes while balancing development, livelihoods, human aspirations and the needs of wildlife. He said the emerging challenges include climate change, increasingly frequent and unpredictable extreme weather events, forest fires, water stress, habitat fragmentation and invasive species, alongside growing pressure on land and natural resources. He called for a landscape approach that brings together forests, wildlife, agriculture, water, livelihoods and human settlements.

Shri Yadav said conservation is not merely a government responsibility but a national responsibility. He described the Forest Service as a service entrusted with the stewardship of India’s natural capital and acknowledged the contribution of frontline forest personnel, including beat guards, rangers and other staff who patrol forests, respond to forest fires and protect wildlife habitats. He said their contribution must never be forgotten and that they are the people who convert conservation policy into conservation on the ground. The Minister said the Eco Warrior Awards celebrate courage without publicity, service without applause and commitment without immediate rewards, and called for the awards to inspire many more people to work for India’s forests, wildlife and environment. He concluded by saying that India’s conservation journey under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi continues to demonstrate to the world that development and environmental stewardship can advance together.

During the awards ceremony, Shri Yadav presented the Lifetime Achievement Award to Shri Brij Kishore Singh, a 1976-batch IFS officer of the Karnataka cadre, in recognition of his decades-long contribution to forest and wildlife conservation. During his career, Singh played an important role in efforts to combat sandalwood smuggling and the activities of notorious brigand Veerappan, besides contributing to forest protection and wildlife conservation in Karnataka.

The awards recognised forest officers and conservation professionals across several categories:

Protected Area Management

Dr. Prakash Chand Gogineni, Conservator of Forests and In-charge Field Director, Similipal Tiger Reserve, Odisha

Dr. Sanjeev Sharma, DCF, Palampur Forest Division, Himachal Pradesh

Environment Conservation

Shri Dharm Singh Meena, Conservator of Forests, Bhagirathi Circle, Uttarakhand

Shri Suman Shivashankar Sivachar W.M., DFO, Wokha, Nagaland

Recognised for scientific water conservation and restoration of springs and streams, and for Amur falcon protection, community engagement and conservation of the Doyang Reservoir.

Community Connect

Shri Dhawan Kumar Rawat, DFO, Pakke Tiger Reserve, Arunachal Pradesh

Shri Gurharsh Singh, DCF, Rampur, Himachal Pradesh

Recognised for linking conservation with community livelihoods and for constructing a timber bridge within six hours following the Samej cloudburst to facilitate rescue operations.

Best Use of Technology

Shri N. Jayaraj, Wildlife Warden, Hosur, Tamil Nadu

Shri Ramsundar M., Director, Rajgir Zoo Safari, Bihar

Recognised for the use of AI-based surveillance and early-warning systems for elephant protection near a vulnerable railway stretch, as well as digital booking, CCTV surveillance and GPS tracking.

Ms. Savita Dahiya, DCF, Barmer, Rajasthan

Ms. K. Karthikeyani, DFO, Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu

Recognised for restoration of Tal Chhapar grassland and improvement of habitat for blackbucks and chinkaras, and for a campaign that removed 239 illegal guns from the landscape while strengthening elephant protection.

Special Projects Recognition

The Special Projects Award recognised Project Elephant and the Great Indian Bustard conservation project in Rajasthan for their significant contributions to species and habitat conservation.

The Eco Warrior Conclave featured three panel discussions focusing on emerging and critical issues in environmental governance and conservation:

AI & Technology for Conservation and Natural Resources Management;

Role of Corporates in Forest Management;

Sustainable Development & Environmental Ethics.

The discussions brought together experts and stakeholders to deliberate on the opportunities and challenges involved in using technology, corporate participation and sustainable development approaches to strengthen conservation outcomes. A photography exhibition showcasing nature photographs captured by civil servants from across India was also organised as part of the event.

The event was attended by eminent personalities from the forestry and conservation sector, including Shri Sushil Kumar Awasthi, DG (Forests) and Special Secretary (MoEFCC); Shri Bharat Lal, Former Secretary General NHRC; Ms. Anita Karn, President, IFSA; Ms. Monalisa Dash, General Secretary, IFSA; and representatives of Indian Masterminds, among other distinguished guests.

headline: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu curtain-raises Routes Asia
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu curtain-raises Routes Asia

23rd Routes Asia to be held from 16-18 March 2027 in New Delhi

29 SEP 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu today unveiled the Curtain Raiser for Routes Asia 2027 in New Delhi, marking a significant milestone in India's preparations to host the prestigious international aviation event. The Curtain Raiser witnessed participation from representatives of 28 embassies, along with leading aviation stakeholders, underscoring the growing international engagement and collaborative opportunities surrounding Routes Asia 2027.

The 24th edition of Routes Asia will be held from 16–18 March 2027 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, bringing together more than 115 leading airlines, representatives from 55+ countries, airports, tourism authorities and aviation stakeholders from across Asia and beyond.

Minister of Civil Aviation, Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, while unveiling the curtain raiser plaque, presented India's vision for Routes Asia 2027 under the theme “Bharat Aviation Rising: Inclusive Growth – Connecting Asia & Beyond.” He highlighted that guided by the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the event comes at an opportune moment as India advances towards becoming the world's third-largest aviation market. He said, “Routes Asia 2027 is coming to the right place, at the right time, with the right opportunity! There is room for more capacity, more airlines and more routes”.

With over 166 airports and plans to develop 100 additional airports over the next decade, India's aviation sector is witnessing rapid expansion. The Minister emphasised the growing importance of the hub-and-spoke model, which can connect more cities and people with emerging markets, creating opportunities for airlines, tourism and economic growth. He also highlighted India's active bilateral aviation engagements, particularly with Southeast Asian countries, and the continued growth in international air travel, with passenger traffic recording a compound annual growth rate of 4.6%.

The Minister extended an invitation to the global aviation community to participate in Routes Asia 2027 and explore India's diverse destinations and expanding aviation opportunities. He underscored the importance of collective stakeholder efforts in connecting Tier-II cities, strengthening international hubs and developing new routes that will shape the next chapter of India's aviation journey.

India formally assumed the hosting responsibilities for Routes Asia 2027 from China West Airport Group during the closing ceremony of Routes Asia 2026 in Xi’an, China, in April 2026, with Airports Authority of India, receiving the hosting baton. The upcoming edition is expected to attract over 2,000 delegates, including decision-makers from leading airlines, airports and tourism authorities.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation, highlighted the transformative role of aviation in connecting people, facilitating trade and creating economic opportunities. Emphasising that international travel should become increasingly accessible and seamless for tourism and business, he underscored the importance of partnerships and route development in strengthening India's aviation ecosystem.

Routes Asia 2027 will provide a strategic platform for strengthening partnerships, developing new air routes and positioning India as a preferred aviation and connectivity destination. The event reinforces India's commitment to inclusive growth, international collaboration and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

headline: Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Launches The Trailer of Documentary Series ‘The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast’
fullText:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region

Union Minister Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Launches The Trailer of Documentary Series ‘The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast’

Landmark cultural outreach initiative by MDoNER and NEC to showcase the Culinary traditions, indigenous communities, and economic potential of all eight Northeastern States.

Series adopts a bottom-up storytelling model, placing local food, farmers, and community traditions at the forefront of regional promotion.

29 SEP 2026 7:03PM by PIB Delhi

The trailer of documentary series “The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast” was officially launched by Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in New Delhi today . The launch event, was organized by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The event was graced by MoS MDoNER Dr. Sukanta Majumdar and attended by senior officials of MDoNER and members of the production team.

The documentary series brings the rich culinary traditions, diverse communities, and vibrant cultural heritage of the eight states of Northeast India into sharp national focus.

Undertaken with the support of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) and the North Eastern Council (NEC), the series has been implemented through the North Eastern Region Community Resource Management Society (NERCRMS) and produced by Urban Media Productions in association with Filandering Forker Media. It marks a significant cultural outreach effort by MDoNER to introduce the Northeast to a wider audience through the experiences and authentic stories of the people of the region.

The documentary series takes viewers on a food-led journey across all eight Northeastern States, exploring the region through its cuisine, communities, and people. The series explores the culinary traditions of the NER rooted in locally available resources, intertwined with interesting facts.

The production of the series involved intraction with local communities and food producers, tracing native ingredients from their origins to kitchens and eventually to the dining table. Through these encounters, the documentary captures not only the food itself, but also the stories, traditions, and people connected to it.

headline: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Completes Preparatory Phase for Special Campaign 6
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Completes Preparatory Phase for Special Campaign 6

Ministry and its organisations also observe “Swachhata Pakhwada” from 16-30 September

MoPSW goals identifies over 11,000 files and 5,624 e-waste items for disposal

29 SEP 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, 29 September 2026: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and its organisations have undertaken extensive preparations for “Special Campaign 6,” the sixth edition of the Government of India's nationwide drive to clean government offices, clear pending work, organise old files and improve institutional efficiency. The preparatory phase of the campaign has run from 15 to 30 September 2026, ahead of the Implementation Phase, which will be carried out from 2 to 31 October, 2026.

Secretary, MoPSW, chaired a review meeting with the Heads of all organisations and Nodal Officers of the Ministry and its organisations to assess preparedness for the campaign. The Secretary emphasised timely action, cleanliness, disposal of pending matters, effective management of e-waste, and proper documentation of activities throughout the campaign.

As part of preparations, MoPSW and its organisations have identified several MP References, References from State Governments, Inter-Ministerial Communications, Parliamentary Assurances, PMO References, Public Grievances and PG Appeals, and Rules/Processes for simplification, along with 185 Cleanliness Campaigns, 6,605 physical files and 4,548 e-files for review and disposal during the campaign. In addition, 5,624 e-waste items have been identified for collection, segregation and disposal in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

MoPSW is coordinating with its organisations through designated Nodal Officers, with progress being reviewed regularly during the Preparatory Phase. The identified activities will now be taken forward in a time-bound manner during the Implementation Phase, from 2 to 31 October 2026, with proper monitoring and documentation of outcomes. An Evaluation Phase, assessing results and best practices from the campaign, is scheduled for 16 to 30 November 2026 under the national framework for Special Campaign 6.

Through Special Campaign 6, MoPSW and all its organisations will undertake concerted efforts towards cleanliness, environmental responsibility, efficient record management, reduction of pendency and responsive governance, with particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.

MoPSW and its organisations are also observing ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ from 16 to 30 September, 2026, coinciding with the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 and reinforcing its cleanliness and public participation objectives. Key activities under ‘Swachhata Pakhwada’ include ‘Shramdaan’ and cleanliness drives, cleaning of public places and community institutions, repair and renovation of toilets, awareness and IEC activities, Waste-to-Wealth exhibitions, ‘Swachhata Raths’ and rallies, cleaning of ponds, rivers and beaches, plantation drives, and elimination of single-use plastic.

headline: NEW CORPORATE AVERAGE FUEL ECONOMY (CAFE) NORMS NOTIFIED
fullText:
Ministry of Power

NEW CORPORATE AVERAGE FUEL ECONOMY (CAFE) NORMS NOTIFIED

SEEKS OVER 16% IMPROVEMENT IN FUEL EFFICIENCY OVER 5 YEARS

SUPPORTS DEVELOPMENT OF ATERNATIVE FUELS, EVs AND HYBRID CARS

PROMOTES INNOVATIONS IN NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR HIGHER ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN CARS

30 SEP 2026 9:57AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Power, Government of India has notified the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) Norms for passenger vehicles, which will come into effect from 1 April 2027 and remain applicable up to 31 March 2032. The new norms will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India.

The new CAFE framework will drive progressive improvements in fuel economy through year-on-year tightening of targets across all five years. The fuel-consumption benchmark is tightened from 3.996 litres/100 km in 2027–28 to 3.3273 litres/100 km in 2031–32, representing an improvement of around 16.7 per cent over the period.

The revised target line has also been flattened to provide a more balanced, weight sensitive approach, with relatively softer targets for lighter vehicles and greater fuel efficiency requirements for heavier vehicles. The reference weight has been increased from 1,082 kg under existing norms to 1,229 kg under new CAFE norms, an increase of around 13.6 per cent, reflecting the evolving characteristics of the passenger vehicle fleet.

The new norms provide flexibility to manufacturers to adopt cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and other innovative solutions. The new CAFE framework promotes technological innovation in new technologies such as Solar reflective paints, advance glazing, high efficiency air-conditioning for improved fuel efficiency and India’s energy security and sustainability objectives.

The passenger vehicle segment accounts for a substantial share of India's transport energy demand and remains an important contributor to fossil-fuel consumption. The new CAFÉ framework is consistent with and supports, rapid technological advancements, increasing availability of alternative and renewable fuels, growing electrification and evolving global automotive technologies.

Explanatory Note

Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) Norms from 2027-28 to 2031-32: A Future-Ready and Flexible Framework for India's Automotive Sector

The new CAFE Norms notified today, will apply to passenger vehicles for the period from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032. They will replace the existing CAFE norms with effect from 1 April 2027 and will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. The new framework provides greater regulatory clarity and a stable policy framework for the automobile industry, while facilitating technological innovation and supporting the continued evolution of India’s passenger vehicle sector towards greater energy efficiency and lower fuel consumption.

CAFE framework marks an important milestone in India’s transition towards cleaner, more energy-efficient and sustainable mobility. The new CAFE Norms have been finalised following extensive consultations with automobile manufacturers, industry associations, academia and other stakeholders, with the objective of providing a future-ready, technology-neutral and flexible regulatory framework for the passenger vehicle sector.

The CAFE framework builds on the gains achieved under the existing regime while providing greater technology choice, flexibility and regulatory certainty to the automotive industry.

The framework seeks to drive continuous improvements in fuel efficiency while enabling greater adoption of cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and innovative solutions, thereby supporting India’s energy security and sustainability objectives. The framework is aligned with the broader vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for clean, energy-efficient and sustainable mobility as an important pillar of India’s development and energy security.

Key Features of the new CAFE Norms

1. The overall fleet-average target has been progressively strengthened compared with the existing targets, while simultaneously providing manufacturers with a range of incentives and compliance pathways to encourage the adoption of clean fuels, cleaner technologies and more efficient vehicles. The framework therefore combines higher ambition with greater flexibility for industry to determine the most appropriate technology pathways.

2. The framework recognises the contribution of renewable and low-carbon fuels, including ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and CBG, through the introduction of the Carbon Neutrality Factor (CNF). This provides manufacturers with an additional pathway for improving their fleet-level CAFE performance, alongside vehicle efficiency improvements and electrification. The provision supports India's broader transition towards cleaner fuels while encouraging innovation across multiple technology pathways.

3. The list of recognised fuel-conservation technologies has been significantly expanded from four to twelve technologies. This provides manufacturers with greater flexibility to adopt and receive recognition for approved fuel-saving technologies. A concession of 1 g CO₂/km for each eligible technology, subject to a maximum of 9.0 g CO₂/km, is available under the framework.

4. Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), Range-Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs), Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs), Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles(SHEV) and Flex-Fuel Vehicles will receive volume derogation factors, also known as ‘super credits’, in fleet-average calculations. This provides an additional incentive for manufacturers to accelerate the deployment and market penetration of cleaner and advanced vehicle technologies.

5. To facilitate ease of compliance and provide manufacturers with greater operational flexibility, manufacturers may opt to meet their obligations over specified two-year/three-year compliance blocks, as provided under the framework. This allows manufacturers greater flexibility in managing their technology transition and product portfolios over the compliance period.

6. The framework provides greater flexibility to manufacturers in meeting their CAFE obligations. Manufacturers that perform better than their prescribed targets will generate credits, which may be carried forward within the specified compliance blocks. Manufacturers with a compliance gap may utilise eligible carry-forward provisions, enter into exchange/trade of credits with other manufacturers, or purchase credits through the buyout mechanism administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. These provisions are intended to ease the compliance burden, provide flexibility during the transition and enable manufacturers to manage variations in their product portfolio and technology adoption pathways.

7. Reporting will be undertaken under both the Modified Indian Driving Cycle (MIDC) and the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP). This dual approach will facilitate India's gradual transition towards globally harmonised vehicle testing practices.

8. Manufacturers with annual sales of below 1,000 units will remain exempt from fleet-average obligations, thereby avoiding the regulatory burden for low-volume manufacturers.
